page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7se.large is an entry-tier virtual server from the Enhanced instance family configured with a compute-focused resource balance. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base clock of 2.9 GHz, the instance delivers 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical execution core using hyper-threading. The hardware platform utilizes the x86_64 architecture and includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. System memory totals 4.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. No local disk storage or GPU accelerators are bundled with the instance, requiring network-attached block storage for persistent data, while external connectivity provides a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread execution alongside throughput constraints inherent to a dual-vCPU allocation. The instance achieves average mid-tier results in single-threaded tasks, scoring 1858.29 in stress-ng and 1559.0 in Geekbench single-core testing. Conversely, multi-threaded results remain in the lowest decile across standardized suites, reflecting a PassMark CPU score of 2990.49 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1813.0 due to the shared single physical core. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 14.89 GB/sec with write throughput at 13.52 GB/sec. Acceleration extensions such as AVX-512, VAES, and SHA_NI provide competent cryptographic and vector math handling, demonstrated by single-threaded gzip compression achieving 27.69 GB/sec.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the ecs.c7se.large involves balancing dedicated CPU consistency against modest aggregate compute and memory capacities. Because the processor allocation is dedicated rather than shared or burstable, it offers stable clock execution without throttling. However, the 4.0 GB memory envelope and absence of local disks prevent large-scale data caching or concurrent parallel pipelines. This profile delivers cost efficiency for microservices, lightweight web servers, task automation runners, small background workers, and staging environments that require consistent processing cycles without extensive multi-threading overhead.
